Do not edit a row to make it pass. A row that fails is dropped and the reason recorded in the results file beside this one.
_rule: The safe-row rule these were written against: no town, spot, day or time; no third party's details; no face, document, account or network detail, health detail or children; a proof the live model check could judge; an honest statement of what the proof can and cannot show; no implied funder; reward marked unfunded draft. All are text-proof rows. Each says how a translator or a language model could answer it and whether that matters to the asker.

candidates.description: Rewrite this app message in plainer words, one sentence: "Your proof is under review." Words only: nothing about you is needed.
candidates.safety: Words only: nothing about you is needed.
candidates.proofKind: text the model can check against the posted line
candidates.checkedBy: the live model check, not a person
candidates.proofShows: Whether the answer is one sentence that keeps the meaning of the posted message in simpler words.
candidates.proofCannotShow: That the sender wrote it. A language model writes a plain rewrite in a second, and nothing tells its answer from a person's.
candidates.machineAnswer: A language model can answer this well. For the asker that matters little if the aim is a pile of candidate rewrites, and a lot if the aim is to learn how real readers would say it.
candidates.whoWouldWantIt: Whoever writes the app's messages and wants plainer wording. A guess, not demand.

candidates.description: Which name fits an app where people do small tasks for points: Favour, Relay or Handy? Pick one and give a reason. Words only: nothing about you is needed.
candidates.safety: Words only: nothing about you is needed.
candidates.proofKind: text the model can check against the posted line
candidates.checkedBy: the live model check, not a person
candidates.proofShows: Whether the answer picks one of the three names and gives a reason that is about the name.
candidates.proofCannotShow: That the sender holds that preference or wrote the reason. A language model picks and argues as easily.
candidates.machineAnswer: A language model can answer, and its pick is not a person's reaction. For the asker that matters a great deal: a naming test is only worth the share of answers that came from people.
candidates.whoWouldWantIt: A builder choosing a product name. A guess, not demand.

candidates.description: An app says: "Verification unavailable, flagged for manual review." Say in your own words what you think happens next. Words only: nothing about you is needed.
candidates.safety: Words only: nothing about you is needed.
candidates.proofKind: text the model can check against the posted line
candidates.checkedBy: the live model check, not a person
candidates.proofShows: Whether the answer says what the reader expects to happen after that message.
candidates.proofCannotShow: That the sender wrote it, or that it is what they really understood. A language model gives the textbook reading, which is exactly what a confused reader would not give.
candidates.machineAnswer: A language model answers this too well. For the asker that matters a great deal: the value is in the wrong guesses of real readers.
candidates.whoWouldWantIt: Whoever writes the app's error messages. This is the message 36 people got on the live app. A guess at demand, not demand.

candidates.description: Which button would you tap to send a photo as proof: "Submit proof" or "Send photo"? Say why in one line. Words only: nothing about you is needed.
candidates.safety: Words only: nothing about you is needed.
candidates.proofKind: text the model can check against the posted line
candidates.checkedBy: the live model check, not a person
candidates.proofShows: Whether the answer picks one of the two labels and gives a reason.
candidates.proofCannotShow: That the sender holds that preference or wrote the reason.
candidates.machineAnswer: A language model can answer. For the asker it matters: a label test wants people's first reaction, and a model's pick is a guess at the average.
candidates.whoWouldWantIt: A designer choosing a button label. A guess, not demand.

candidates.description: A new app: "Ask verified humans small questions, they answer for points." In one line, what is your first doubt? Words only: nothing about you is needed.
candidates.safety: Words only: nothing about you is needed.
candidates.proofKind: text the model can check against the posted line
candidates.checkedBy: the live model check, not a person
candidates.proofShows: Whether the answer states a doubt about the described app.
candidates.proofCannotShow: That the sender wrote it or holds that doubt.
candidates.machineAnswer: A language model lists plausible doubts easily. For the asker that matters somewhat: the list is still useful, the ranking by how many people said it is not.
candidates.whoWouldWantIt: A builder testing a one-line pitch before launch. A guess, not demand.

candidates.description: Read this: "Tap Claim, do the favour, send proof." Which one word is hardest for a new reader, and what would you use? Words only: nothing about you is needed.
candidates.safety: Words only: nothing about you is needed.
candidates.proofKind: text the model can check against the posted line
candidates.checkedBy: the live model check, not a person
candidates.proofShows: Whether the answer names one word that is in the posted sentence and offers another word for it.
candidates.proofCannotShow: That the sender wrote it, or found that word hard.
candidates.machineAnswer: A language model can answer. For the asker it matters somewhat: a model can spot jargon, but not which word really stops a new reader.
candidates.whoWouldWantIt: Whoever writes onboarding text and wants it readable by people new to the language or to apps. A guess, not demand.

candidates.description: Translate for a sign-in screen, and name the language: "Prove you are human once. Stay private always." Words only: nothing about you is needed.
candidates.safety: Words only: nothing about you is needed.
candidates.proofKind: text the model can check against the posted line
candidates.checkedBy: the live model check, not a person
candidates.proofShows: Whether the text is a fair translation of the posted line into the language named.
candidates.proofCannotShow: That the sender speaks the language or wrote it. A machine translation passes.
candidates.machineAnswer: A translator answers it. For the asker that matters little if any correct translation will do, and a lot if the aim is wording a native speaker would choose.
candidates.whoWouldWantIt: A team translating a sign-in screen. A guess, not demand.

candidates.description: Put these four steps in the order that makes sense: send proof, read the task, earn points, claim the task. Words only: nothing about you is needed.
candidates.safety: Words only: nothing about you is needed.
candidates.proofKind: text the model can check against the posted line
candidates.checkedBy: the live model check, not a person
candidates.proofShows: Whether the answer lists the four posted steps in an order.
candidates.proofCannotShow: That the sender worked it out. There is one sensible order and a language model gives it at once.
candidates.machineAnswer: A language model gets it right every time. For the asker that matters completely: the only use of this row is to see where people get the order wrong.
candidates.whoWouldWantIt: A designer checking whether the flow is obvious. A guess, not demand.

candidates.description: Rewrite this so it is kind and still clear: "Proof not accepted. Try again." One or two short sentences. Words only: nothing about you is needed.
candidates.safety: Words only: nothing about you is needed.
candidates.proofKind: text the model can check against the posted line
candidates.checkedBy: the live model check, not a person
candidates.proofShows: Whether the answer keeps the meaning of the posted message and is at most two sentences.
candidates.proofCannotShow: That the sender wrote it. Whether it is kind is a judgement the model makes, not a fact.
candidates.machineAnswer: A language model writes this well. For the asker that matters little: a good rewrite is a good rewrite, whoever wrote it.
candidates.whoWouldWantIt: Whoever writes the app's rejection message. A guess, not demand.

candidates.description: What do you think "Claim" means on a button in a tasks app? Answer in one line, before you look anything up. Words only: nothing about you is needed.
candidates.safety: Words only: nothing about you is needed.
candidates.proofKind: text the model can check against the posted line

candidates.machineAnswer: A language model gives the intended meaning. For the asker that matters a great deal: the value is in the readings that differ from it.
candidates.whoWouldWantIt: A designer checking one word on one button. A guess, not demand.

candidates.description: For a five minute task, which would you rather have: 10 points now or 15 points next week? Pick one and say why. Words only: nothing about you is needed.
